ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Ada Lovelace

code.originalText: Two-week follow-up and gynecologic oncology consultation: pathology, MRI and PET-CT, staging, treatment intent, palliative care, and long-acting morphine

text.paragraph: Two-week follow-up of abnormal bleeding and pelvic pain, with the biopsy, MRI and PET-CT results and gynecologic oncology consultation today. [S]

Mrs. Lovelace returns two weeks after her first visit, on the day of her consultation with Dr. Lindgren-Osei. She stopped the opium tincture as agreed and takes oral morphine solution 5 mg with the oral syringe, about six doses a day; her average pelvic pain over the past week is 6 of 10, and she is not drowsy. The bleeding continues, lighter than before, with a watery discharge. She is a little less breathless on stairs since the iron infusion. Her bowels open every other day on senna and polyethylene glycol. She had the MRI a week ago and the PET-CT five days ago. She asked to hear all the results herself and plainly. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-16; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Pale and alert; blood pressure 106/66, pulse 92, weight 54.2 kg
No supraclavicular or inguinal lymph node enlargement
Soft; mild suprapubic tenderness; no masses or liver enlargement

Bleeding between periods and after intercourse, with heavier periods, a watery blood-stained discharge and a constant pelvic ache, for about five months; average pain 7 of 10 despite her opium tincture; a friable cervical mass found on examination and biopsied; cause not yet established at intake
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented final illness; superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss: hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL, mean cell volume 74 fL, ferritin 5 ng/mL, with tiredness and breathlessness on stairs
S — Synthetic modern finding anchored to her documented final illness.

Adenocarcinoma of the endocervix, usual (HPV-associated) type, HPV 18 positive, FIGO 2018 stage IVB: a 5.2 cm tumor with left parametrial invasion, metastases to left pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes, and bilateral lung metastases on MRI and PET-CT; PD-L1 combined positive score 5, mismatch repair proficient, HER2 1+; treated with palliative pelvic radiation for bleeding and carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab, with specialist palliative care from diagnosis
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit, anchored to her documented uterine cancer; the cervical site is a synthetic choice.
Cancer-related pelvic pain, nociceptive and visceral, from the cervical tumor and its left parametrial extension
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit.

Long-term prescribed opioid therapy: opium tincture for recurrent pelvic and abdominal pain for about two years, measured at times with a household spoon, converted at intake to measured oral morphine; no opioid use disorder on a DSM-5 assessment; naloxone supplied
S — Synthetic modern history anchored to her documented laudanum and opium; not a claim about her real dosing.

list.item:
Adenocarcinoma of the cervix, FIGO 2018 stage IVB (C53.0). The bleeding and pain now have their explanation. The cervical biopsy shows invasive adenocarcinoma of usual (HPV-associated) type, HPV 18 positive, with PD-L1 combined positive score 5, mismatch repair proficient, and HER2 1+. MRI shows a 5.2 cm tumor with left parametrial invasion; PET-CT shows avid left pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes and six nodules in both lungs. This is stage IVB by imaging. HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C tests before treatment are negative. Dr. Lindgren-Osei and I told her the diagnosis together, as she asked: the cancer cannot be cured, and treatment aims to control it, stop the bleeding and relieve pain, and help her live longer and well. [S]
CT-guided biopsy of a lung nodule to confirm metastatic disease.
Palliative pelvic radiation, 20 Gy in 5 fractions, next week, for bleeding and pain.
Then carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab every 3 weeks; bevacizumab not used while she is bleeding and after pelvic radiation.
No germline genetic testing.
Specialist palliative care starting today.

Cancer-related pelvic pain (G89.3). Average 6 of 10 on about 30 mg of oral morphine a day in divided doses, without sedation. Constant pain needs a long-acting opioid. [S]
Long-acting morphine 15 mg every 12 hours.
Oral morphine solution 5 mg every 4 hours as needed for breakthrough pain.
Continue acetaminophen 1 g three times a day and the laxatives every day.

Iron deficiency anemia from blood loss (D50.0). Hemoglobin 9.0 g/dL, from 8.4, two weeks after the first iron infusion, with bleeding continuing; no transfusion needed. [S]
Second ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg infusion today.
Ferritin 6 to 8 weeks from now.

Long-term opioid therapy (Z79.891). Using the measured morphine as directed, from this one prescriber; no signs of opioid use disorder. [S]
Naloxone at home; morphine in a locked box.
Prescription monitoring program checked: no other prescribers.
